subject: design-studies
title: Ergonomic Dimensions: Fit the Chair and Desk to the Student

segments.say: Measure the student first. The lower-leg height is 40 cm, the hip breadth is 36 cm, and the seated elbow rests 24 cm above the seat - and the fit bar starts empty, because nothing has been sized yet. Point at the three measurements on your student notes before anything is built.
questions: What three measurements are taken from the student?
Why does the fit bar start empty?

segments.say: Set the seat height. The seat rises until it equals the lower-leg height of 40 cm: the feet rest flat, the gap under the thigh closes, and the fit bar climbs to one third. Now try the seat-height question on your worksheet.
questions: Which measurement set the seat height?
What closed when the seat reached 40 cm?

segments.say: Set the seat width and the desk height from the body. The seat widens to hip breadth plus clearance, 36 + 4 cm, and the desk top settles at seat height plus seated elbow height, 40 + 24 = 64 cm, so the forearms rest level and the fit bar climbs to two thirds. Check both sums against your student notes before moving on.
questions: How is the seat width calculated?
Why is the desk height built up from the seat height?

segments.say: The wrong turn, then the fix. A standard chair built to average measurements leaves this student feet dangling and the desk too high; the fitted sizes are then restored - seat, width and desk each set from the student own measurements - and the fit bar fills. Keep the three measurements in view as you check your student notes and finish the exit ticket.
questions: What goes wrong with the standard size?
Which measurement sets each dimension in the fitted chair?
segments.watchFor: One standard size fits every user, because a chair built to average measurements fits each person who sits in it. Listen for students who reach for a standard or average size instead of the measurements. Send them back to the three measurements: Ergonomic design sizes the product from the user's own measurements: the seat height is set to the lower-leg height so the feet rest flat, the seat width to the hip breadth plus clearance, and the desk height to the seat height plus the seated elbow height - a chair built to the average leaves every gap open for anyone who is not average.
